summary: PASS — Static analysis + runtime smoke test on AppLockGate.tsx (biometric debug logging + widened debounce guard). All 12 required [AppLock] log strings present (21 total console.log occurrences). Guards verified: 3000ms debounce in maybeLock (line 103), bioBusyRef guard (line 158), sessionUnlockedRef guard (line 162), render uses `!locked || sessionUnlockedRef.current` (line 234). Lint: 0 errors. action_items: Ship to real device and capture `adb logcat -s ReactNativeJS:V | grep '\[AppLock\]'` when the user reproduces the 'fingerprint SUCCESS but stays locked' bug. The full trace (biometricPrompt returned → SUCCESS → commitUnlock → 3× setLocked(false) → render CHILDREN) will pinpoint whether the bug is in the promise resolution, setState batching, or a stale AppState 'inactive' event firing during the prompt overlay (which the 3s debounce now guards against).
critical_code_review_comments: Debug console.logs are intentionally verbose for on-device diagnosis. Recommend gating them behind a `if (__DEV__)` check or a `LOG_APPLOCK` flag before production release so they don't bloat logcat / cost cycles in release builds.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 16 verified debug-logging + 3s debounce fix in AppLockGate.tsx. Next iteration should be triggered ONLY after the user tests on a real device and provides adb logcat output. The exact log sequence expected on successful biometric unlock is: AppState active→X→active → maybeLock (should be skipped by debounce if within 3s) → tryBiometric: starting → biometricPrompt returned {success:true} → SUCCESS — calling commitUnlock → commitUnlock() called → setLocked(false) 1/3, 2/3, 3/3 → render: locked=false → CHILDREN.
rca_of_issue: Still pending real-device confirmation. Hypothesis being instrumented: OEM (Realme/Poco/OnePlus) fires a spurious AppState 'inactive'→'active' cycle when the native biometric overlay dismisses, causing maybeLock() to re-run right after commitUnlock() flips setLocked(false). The widened 3s debounce (was 1s) + sessionUnlockedRef sticky flag + 3× setLocked(false) via immediate/setTimeout/rAF should now cover this. Logcat trace will confirm whether the theory is correct or if a different path (e.g. biometricPrompt promise never resolving with success) is at fault.
